claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024 reports: A 2024 stakeholder workshop framed water scarcity and artisanal mining as contributors to resource tensions, and identified climate-related livelihood shocks, displacement and harmful coping as pathways that may destabilize communities and strain host-area services.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: A workshop-derived shared-vision summary, not tested causal mechanisms, a named local conflict case or evidence of climate-caused violence.

executive_assessment.text: Named vulnerability examples include Zvimba crops, Sanyati service access and water-point pressures primarily in Masvingo/Matabeleland South/Midlands, all explicitly dated.
Mwenezi, Chipinge and Makoholi provide concrete reported adaptation/governance inputs; their outcomes are not independently evaluated.
Protection risks and stakeholder climate-security pathways remain qualitative assessments rather than measured climate-caused violence.
